channel.title: Kemeya Azezi: Blog
channel.description: Notes, tasting impressions and things worth learning about tea and coffee, from Kemeya Azezi.

item.title: Why Matcha Is Grown in the Dark Before It's Ever Ground
item.description: Matcha isn't just green tea in powder form. Shading the bushes for weeks, steaming without rolling, and grinding by stone instead of blade each shape the final cup before it's whisked.

item.title: How Pu-erh Actually Ferments, and Why Raw and Ripe Are Barely the Same Tea
item.description: Sheng and shou pu-erh start as the same leaf, but one ages slowly for years while the other is fermented on purpose in under two months. The difference is a 1973 invention, not tradition.

item.title: How Coffee Actually Gets Decaffeinated, and Why It's Never Fully Caffeine-Free
item.description: Decaffeination isn't one process. Water, carbon dioxide and chemical solvents each pull caffeine out of the bean differently, and every method still leaves a small amount behind.

item.title: The Insect Bite Behind Darjeeling's Most Prized Flavour
item.description: Darjeeling's four seasonal flushes produce genuinely different teas from the same bushes, and the most famous one owes its flavour to a tiny insect the growers don't fully get rid of.

item.title: What "Orange Pekoe" Actually Means (It's Not a Flavour)
item.description: Orange Pekoe isn't a tea variety or a citrus flavour: it's a leaf grade, part of a whole sorting system that has nothing to do with taste.

item.title: Water Temperature Is the Most Underrated Variable in a Cup of Tea
item.description: Why boiling water ruins delicate teas, the right temperature for each style, and simple ways to get it right without a thermometer.
